findings.body: `deleted_paths_under` counts any path ever deleted in history, even if a later commit saved it again. If the user deletes a tracked file, saves, then recreates the file, `live_matches_saved` sees it as an addition that is in `deleted` and returns false. The entry is then treated as held, so the recreated file is probably not captured or published until a pull releases it. Consider only counting deletions that are not followed by a re-add, or deletions that did not originate from this machine's own checkpoints.

live_matches_saved now returns true whenever every saved file is live and unchanged, ignoring live files with no saved version. That also covers a file another machine deleted and pulled into the saved version but not yet applied locally. The stream is then treated as held, and the next capture re-saves the file, silently reverting the remote deletion. Before this change the live/saved set mismatch made the stream unheld, so the capture carried the pulled version and the deletion was applied. The check needs a way to tell a widened-entry addition from a remotely deleted file, for example by only ignoring live files that no previous narrower stream covered, or files not present in the upstream history.
findings.statusReason: Fixed in 58b789e5d2: extra live files only count as additions when no stream held here covered them; e2e test_dotfiles_profile_remote_deletion reproduces the scenario.

trail.title: fix(dotfiles): keep saving a directory tracked in place of narrower paths
